articles.title: China starts construction of innovative nuclear project
articles.summary: First concrete has been poured for the nuclear island of unit 1 at Phase I of the Xuwei nuclear power project in China's Jiangsu province. The plant will supply both industrial heating and electricity by coupling a high-temperature gas-cooled reactor with two Hualong One pressurised water reactors.

articles.title: Project Phoenix report backs SMR use in Slovakia
articles.summary: A feasibility study carried out as part of the USA's Project Phoenix scheme has backed the suitability of small modular reactors in the Slovak Republic.

articles.title: National targets for new nuclear 'far exceed a tripling of global capacity'
articles.summary: Global generating capacity could reach 1,446 GWe by 2050 if governments hit their targets for new nuclear, far exceeding the 1,200 GWe goal set in the Declaration to Triple Nuclear Energy, according to a new World Nuclear Association report.

articles.title: Joint study validates SMR use for chemical plants
articles.summary: A two-year study by Oak Ridge National Laboratory and NuScale looked at the performance and profitability of coupling a NuScale Power Module with a US chemical facility to provide nuclear-generated steam and electric power - and shows pairing NuScale's nuclear technology with a heat augmentation system to be both profitable and reliable.

articles.title: Slovakia and USA sign nuclear energy agreement
articles.summary: Slovakia's Prime Minister Robert Fico and US Energy Secretary Chris Wright have signed an Intergovernmental Agreement to advance the European country's nuclear power programme, including deploying a new 1,200 MWe unit.

articles.title: UK maritime nuclear consortium launched
articles.summary: Lloyd's Register is leading a new consortium of UK companies seeking "to set the highest international standards for safe, secure and commercially viable nuclear-powered ships".

articles.summary: The first nuclear units in Bangladesh and Turkey, plus ones at Tianwan and Xudabao in China could all start-up during 2026, according to Rosatom Director General Alexei Likhachev.

articles.title: Dioxitek celebrates record UO2 production
articles.summary: Argentina's state-owned producer of uranium dioxide set a new production record in 2025, which it says means it is possible to meet the needs of the country's nuclear power plants domestically.

articles.title: Tepco delays restart of Kashiwazaki-Kariwa reactor

articles.summary: Western Canada's first Small Modular Reactor Safety, Licensing, and Testing Centre at the University of Regina is to receive nearly CAD6 million (USD4.3 million) in funding from the federal and provincial governments.

articles.title: KHNP takes stake in TerraPower

articles.title: Cooling system tests at RA-10 multipurpose reactor

articles.title: International safety assessments of Finnish, French SMRs
articles.summary: Nuclear safety authorities from the Czech Republic, Finland, Poland, Sweden, and Ukraine are conducting a Joint Early Review to assess the safety of Steady Energy's LDR-50 reactor for district heating. Meanwhile, the third phase of a review of safety options for France's Nuward SMR has been started by eight European nuclear regulators.

articles.title: Tepco halts restart of Kashiwazaki-Kariwa reactor
articles.summary: Japan's Tokyo Electric Power Company has temporarily shut down unit 6 at its Kashiwazaki-Kariwa nuclear power plant after an alarm was triggered in the control rod operation monitoring system. Before Wednesday's restart, the unit had been offline for almost 14 years.

articles.title: First VVER-1200 fuel delivered to China for Tianwan 7
